潰.meaning: A mouse keeps one <part>precious</part> blueberry in a thimble, polishing it every night. Then a cloudburst of <part>water drops</part> hammers down, each one the size of a melon, and splat: the berry is a purple puddle. Even rain can <kanji>crush</kanji>.
潰.on: Next storm she ties her berries to a <sound>ki</sound>te and flies them above the clouds.
潰.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the soggy mouse, and dries off with a page of her <sound>boo</sound>k.

簿.meaning: Every player at the pond's <part>water polo</part> club must sign a long <part>bamboo</part> scroll before they swim. The frogs sign with wet feet, the ducks with a beak dipped in ink. That dripping scroll is the club's <kanji>register</kanji>.
簿.on: It is kept in the clubhouse beside a tiny <sound>bo</sound>nsai.

傑.meaning: A wooden puppet with <part>mismatched legs</part>, one long and one short, is laughed at by every toy. He climbs the tallest <part>tree</part> anyway and hangs his cap on the <part>coat hook</part> nailed at the top for heroes. Wobbly legs, true <kanji>greatness</kanji>.
傑.on: The toys say sorry with a hot dog smothered in <sound>ketch</sound>up.
傑.kun: They serve him <sound>su</sound>shi too and shout, '<sound>Goo</sound>d job!'

悼.meaning: A writer's beloved old <part>desk</part> finally collapses with woodworm. She drapes it in black, lays her pencils on it like flowers and hums a slow tune, her <part>heartbeat</part> heavy. Forty years of novels. She stays up all night to <kanji>lament</kanji> it.
悼.on: Leaving, she stubs her <sound>toe</sound> on its broken leg and cries even harder.
悼.kun: Friends come to the wake with an <sound>ee</sound>l pie and a <sound>ta</sound>co platter.

肺.meaning: At a night <part>market</part>, one stall sells jars of fresh mountain air. The <part>moon</part> buys a dozen, takes a huge breath and swells to twice its size, glowing pink. Two big air bags puff in and out inside it: it has <kanji>lungs</kanji>.
肺.on: Its sigh blows a <sound>hi</sound>ve off the next stall, and the bees chase it home.

鋳.meaning: For her hundredth birthday, a toast to her <part>longevity</part>, Grandma gets a statue. Glowing <part>gold</part> is poured into a mould of her, hissing and spitting. When the mould cracks open, a shiny little Grandma gleams back. That's <kanji>casting</kanji>.
鋳.on: The sculptor seals one crack in the mould with a blob of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum.
鋳.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k, it's still hot!' squeals the real Grandma, poking its golden nose.

詐.meaning: A salesman gives a grand <part>speech</part> at the fair: his <part>coat rack</part> is a magic tree that grows a fresh coat every night. People pay a fortune. Next morning every rack is bare, apart from one sock he hung there himself. The whole thing was a <kanji>lie</kanji>.
詐.on: He runs off with the money hidden in a <sound>sa</sound>rdine tin.
詐.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' he shrieks, sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and slips in a puddle of <sound>wa</sound>sabi as the crowd chases him.

欺.meaning: A librarian lets out a huge <part>yawn</part> and pretends to doze. A thief tiptoes up to the <part>bookshelf</part> for the rare book, and the whole shelf swings round, spinning him into a locked cupboard. The sleepy librarian was pure <kanji>deceit</kanji>.
欺.on: The trick shelf turns on a giant hidden <sound>gear</sound>.
欺.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' yells the thief, stuck in the dark with a rug from a ba<sound>za</sound>ar and a stuffed <sound>moo</sound>se head.

硫.meaning: Near a hot spring, a <part>squid</part> wraps its arms round a bright yellow <part>stone</part> and won't let go. Every diver who swims by holds their nose: the rock smells of rotten eggs. The squid adores it. Its treasure is a lump of <kanji>sulphur</kanji>.
硫.on: It brings the stone to every family <sound>reu</sound>nion, and everyone groans.

愉.meaning: A retired astronaut builds a little <part>spaceship</part> in his garden for the neighbourhood cats. They curl up in it in the sun, purring so loud he can feel each <part>heartbeat</part> through the hull. He watches with his tea, grinning: pure <kanji>pleasure</kanji>.
愉.on: He rolls the cats a <sound>yu</sound>zu to bat around the cockpit.
愉.kun: He munches a <sound>ta</sound>co and sighs, '<sound>No</sound>t a bad life.'

擦.meaning: The ship's cook has lost her cheese grater, so she ties a block of cheese to the <part>anchor</part> and drags it along the rocky seabed. As it comes up, the crew <part>guess</part> how much is left: just a bag of fluffy shreds. A rocky sea is a fine way to <kanji>grate</kanji>.
擦.on: She also grates the peel of a <sound>sats</sound>uma over the top.
擦.kun: Then she rubs a little of the cheese onto a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi.

縛.meaning: A <part>tennis player</part> keeps losing because her socks slip down. Her coach, a retired chef, winds strong <part>thread</part> round her ankles, knees and waist like a holiday roast. She can only hop to the net, but nothing slips. He sure knows how to <kanji>truss</kanji>.
縛.on: He adds a belt with a huge <sound>buc</sound>kle, just in case.
縛.kun: Her opponent, a <sound>shee</sound>p, laughs so hard it drops its <sound>bu</sound>ttered toast.

冗.meaning: A kind aunt knits a <part>blanket</part> for her <part>table</part> so it won't catch cold, then a scarf for each leg, then four little hats and a hot water bottle. The table never asked for any of it. Every stitch is <kanji>superfluous</kanji>.
冗.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey hops out of the pile wearing one of the hats.

渓.meaning: A puppeteer lowers her <part>marionette</part> on a string, metres and metres down between two cliffs, to fill its tiny bucket from the stream far below. Cold <part>water drops</part> splash its painted face. She's never needed so much string as for this deep <kanji>ravine</kanji>.
渓.on: At the bottom it finds a picnic: a slice of birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke on a rock.
渓.kun: It comes back up with a <sound>ta</sound>co balanced on one wooden <sound>knee</sound>.

塔.meaning: Every year a family stacks one more <part>picnic basket</part> on the same mound of <part>soil</part>, each with a curved, roof-shaped lid. After a century the stack is ten storeys high, with bells on every lid. Tourists climb it, sure it's a <kanji>pagoda</kanji>.
塔.on: A boy at the top balances on one big <sound>toe</sound> to ring the highest bell.

悠.meaning: A <part>fan seller</part> has kept the same stall on the same bridge for five hundred years. Kings, trams and shops come and go; his kind <part>heart</part> stays the same, and so does his price. He's less a man than a piece of <kanji>permanence</kanji>.
悠.on: His only customer as old as he is is a <sound>u</sound>nicorn, who buys one fan each century.

俺.meaning: In a rough biker bar, someone has hung a frilly pink <part>parasol</part> on the <part>coat hook</part>. 'Whose is this?' growls the barman. The biggest biker stands up, thumps his chest and says, 'Mine. <kanji>I</kanji> love it.'
俺.on: He rides off with it open above him, his <sound>en</sound>gine roaring.
俺.kun: An <sound>o</sound>tter rides behind him on the seat, holding a <sound>re</sound>d balloon.

閥.meaning: Five lumberjacks <part>fell</part> trees only for each other. They build a private <part>gate</part> from the logs and give a key to nobody else. Inside, they wear matching checked shirts and laugh at their own jokes. Outsiders call them a <kanji>clique</kanji>.
閥.on: To join, you need a secret <sound>bu</sound>tton sewn onto your shirt.

閲.meaning: At the castle <part>gate</part>, a fussy <part>imp</part> with a magnifying glass checks every visitor: their boots, their hats, the spelling in their letters. Mistakes get a red mark. Nobody gets in until he has done a full <kanji>review</kanji>.
閲.on: The best guests get a tiny <sound>etch</sound>ing of the castle as a prize.
閲.kun: Those who pass get tea from a <sound>ke</sound>ttle carried by a <sound>mee</sound>rkat.

岳.meaning: A <part>hill</part> wanted to be taller, so it climbed on top of a <part>mountain</part>, like a kid on its dad's shoulders. Together they poke right through the clouds and end in one needle-sharp <kanji>point</kanji>, where eagles queue to perch on the peak.
岳.on: A <sound>ga</sound>ggle of geese lands on the tip and squabbles over who's highest.
岳.kun: A climber at the top unpacks a <sound>ta</sound>co and a little <sound>ke</sound>ttle.

桃.meaning: A fortune teller reads the future in fruit, not tea leaves. She plucks one from her <part>tree</part>, studies its fuzz and finds a <part>portent</part>: 'You'll be sticky by noon.' She bites in and juice runs down her chin. It came true: a <kanji>peach</kanji>.
桃.on: A drop of juice lands on her bare big <sound>toe</sound>.
桃.kun: She wipes it up with a <sound>mo</sound>p, while a <sound>mo</sound>th sips the last drop.

克.meaning: For years the <part>old</part> tug-of-war champion has beaten every <part>big brother</part> in the village. This year one skinny big brother trains all winter, drags him over the mud line, and helps him up with a bow. Fear, mud and a legend: he managed to <kanji>overcome</kanji> them all.
克.on: A <sound>coc</sound>katoo on the fence screeches the new champion's name.
克.kun: He keeps perfectly <sound>ca</sound>lm for one second, then dances in the mud: to win.

奔.meaning: A <part>large</part> man sleeps in and runs for the train with a whole <part>bush</part> still tangled in his beard from his camping trip. Leaves fly, pigeons scatter, porters leap aside. His dash sets the whole station into a <kanji>bustle</kanji>.
奔.on: Taxis outside join in, <sound>hon</sound>king their horns.
奔.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs a <sound>shee</sound>p in the next carriage as he sprints past.

犠.meaning: A <part>cow</part> wins the blue ribbon at the fair, then sees that the judges cheated a little goat out of it. Out of pure <part>justice</part>, she hands the ribbon over and walks home with nothing. Giving up what you love for what's right: <kanji>sacrifice</kanji>.
犠.on: The goat thanks her by fixing the broken <sound>gear</sound> on her milking machine.
犠.kun: At home she has an <sound>ee</sound>l pie, a <sound>ke</sound>ttle of tea, a rug over her <sound>knee</sound>s and one boiled <sound>e</sound>gg.

牲.meaning: In a dry summer, a <part>cow</part> has grown just one flower in her whole field, the only bit of <part>life</part> left. She carries it gently in her mouth to the village shrine and leaves it there for the rain gods. Her one flower is her <kanji>sacrifice</kanji>.
牲.on: That night the rain comes, and the priest locks the flower in a <sound>sa</sound>fe.

伯.meaning: Everyone in the office hangs a grey coat on the <part>coat hook</part>, except for one long <part>white</part> coat with gold buttons. When it's there, everyone whispers and works faster. Nobody needs to see who wears it: it belongs to the <kanji>chief</kanji>.
伯.on: Its pocket always holds a slice of <sound>huc</sound>kleberry pie.

爵.meaning: The queen runs a grabber game at the palace: a metal <part>claw</part> dangles over a <part>net</part> full of titles. A <part>robot</part> pays one coin, the claw lifts a scroll, and the queen taps its shoulder with a <part>golf club</part>, for lack of a sword. Arise, Lord Robot, <kanji>baron</kanji>.
爵.on: His new castle has a moat with a friendly <sound>shar</sound>k.

寡.meaning: Under her <part>roof</part>, an old lady has turned a red <part>phone booth</part> into a shrine to her late husband, a pirate. <part>One</part> parrot perches on top, his <part>sword</part> hangs inside with <part>eight</part> roses below it. Every evening she rings him for a chat: the cheerful <kanji>widow</kanji>.
寡.on: Afterwards she feeds his old pet <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond.

朱.meaning: A young tree, <part>not yet</part> tall enough for fruit, is jealous of the apple trees. So a painter gives it one quick <part>slash</part> of orange-red across its top branch. Now it glows brighter than any apple: pure <kanji>vermilion</kanji>.
朱.on: Ants march up its trunk, sure the paint is made of <sound>su</sound>gar.
朱.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' sighs the painter, and puts the <sound>ke</sound>ttle on to celebrate.

糧.meaning: Before her trek to the Pole, an explorer weighs every grain of <part>rice</part> on her scales: the exact <part>quantity</part> for three hundred days, packed into sacks on forty sleds. The huskies eye it hungrily. Her sleds are loaded with <kanji>provisions</kanji>.
糧.on: On the way she stops at a cosy <sound>ryo</sound>kan, and the cook adds one more sack for free.
糧.kun: In the <sound>ca</sound>lm of a snowy night she counts the sacks in her <sound>te</sound>nt.
